What it shows
How it works
Good to know
More
Your week
Workouts you finished in the last 7 days, compared with the sessions per week you chose in your profile.
A workout counts once you finish it. The ring fills toward your weekly number. The button starts a new workout or resumes the one in progress.
The weekly number is your own choice, not a recommendation. Training you did not log is unknown, not missed.
Food today
Calories and protein from the meals you logged today, and how your logged calories split between protein, carbs and fat.
Totals add up every entry for today. Progress rings appear only when you enter your own calorie or protein target in your profile.
A day may be only partly logged. Forma never sets or changes your targets.
A small next step
One short suggestion about what to record next.
Fixed rules check the last 7 days in order: a first workout, food on at least 3 days, weight on at least 3 days, then workouts against your weekly number. It works offline, without AI.
It is about keeping records, not a training or diet instruction, and it never changes your plan.
Recorded milestones
Badges for totals you have reached: your first finished workout and working-set counts such as 10, 100 and 1,000.
Counted from your log. Warm-up sets are not included.
Milestones count records. They do not measure fitness or progress.
Food for the day
Totals for the selected date from the entries you logged, next to your own targets if you set them.
Change the date to view or log another day. Each entry keeps the values it was logged with.
Only what you logged is included. Missing entries are unknown, and a logged day may be incomplete.
Add food
Ways to log food: quick re-log, your saved foods and recipes, online lookup, or typing the values yourself.
Pick the meal first (breakfast, lunch, dinner, snacks, suhoor, iftar or unassigned). Each entry saves its own copy of the nutrition values.
Older entries without a meal stay unassigned. Forma never guesses meal times.
Quick re-log
The meals you log most often for the chosen meal, ready to log again with one tap.
Ranked by how often you logged each name; ties keep the most recent. Tapping copies the values from your latest entry of that meal.
Built only from your own history; nothing is suggested from outside.
Online food search
Packaged foods found by name or barcode in Open Food Facts, a free public database.
Only your search words or barcode are sent. Choosing a result adds it to My foods, where you can check or edit it before logging a portion. It needs an internet connection.
Entries are added by the public (ODbL licence) and may be wrong or incomplete, so compare them with the label. Logging works offline without this.
My foods and recipes
Foods you saved from labels and recipes you built from them.
A recipe adds up its ingredients and divides the total by the servings you enter. Logging a food copies its values into that meal.
Editing or deleting a saved food never changes meals or recipes already saved. Nothing is preloaded.
Water
Water you logged for the selected day, next to your own daily water target if you set one.
Each button adds the amount shown to that day\'s total.
The target is your own input. Forma does not suggest how much to drink.
Supplements & vitamins
A personal daily checklist for the vitamins or supplements you choose to track.
Add a name and an optional dose note, then tick it off each day.
A checklist only, not medical or dosage advice. Deleting an item also removes its history.
Programs
Workout templates: ready-made starter programs and programs you create.
Starting a program copies its exercises, targets, rest time and notes into a new workout, so later edits to the program do not change past workouts.
Starter programs are editable logging templates, not personal prescriptions. Choose exercises and loads that suit your routine.
Logging sets
Record each set with reps, load and optional effort (RPE), and mark warm-up sets separately.
Warm-ups stay out of records, charts, volume and targets. In a superset or circuit, working sets move through the group and rest starts when the round ends. The rest timer uses the time you chose.
RPE is how hard a set felt to you (0 to 10). Forma never prescribes a load from it.
Finish workout
Ends the current workout and saves it to your history.
Only finished workouts count in your week, calendar, records, muscle maps and trends. An unfinished workout stays open so you can resume it.
A workout needs at least one logged set before it can be finished.
Exercise guide
How a movement looks: start and end images, a 3D figure or video for some exercises, form cues and the muscles involved.
Highlighted muscles come from Forma\'s exercise catalog, with primary and supporting muscles shown separately. With reduced motion on, moving guides stay still until you press play.
Images are AI-generated illustrations, not personal coaching. Colours mark catalogued muscles, not measured activation.
Exercise load history
One exercise over time: your heaviest working load or your estimated one-rep max for each workout.
Estimated 1RM uses the Epley formula, load × (1 + reps ÷ 30), on loaded working sets of 1 to 15 reps. Each point is a recorded workout; gaps are not filled in.
An estimate is not a tested maximum. Warm-ups are excluded.
Weekly muscles
Working sets from finished workouts in the last 7 days, grouped by muscle.
Each exercise counts toward its primary muscles and, separately, its supporting muscles from the catalog.
These are catalog associations, not recovery scores, and the two counts should not be added together.
Recent sessions
Your latest finished workouts with their sets.
Open a workout to review its sets, or repeat it to start a new workout with the same exercises, targets and rest time.
A repeated workout starts with no sets, so you log what you actually do.
My custom exercises
Movements you add yourself, such as a specific machine or speciality lift.
Give it a name, primary muscle and equipment, then log sets for it like any other exercise.
Custom exercises have no guide images. Deleting one also deletes its recorded sets.
Cardio and timed activity
Activities you time yourself, such as a run, a ride, rowing or a plank hold.
Pick the activity, enter the time and, if you like, the distance. The 7-day line adds up only what you logged; pace for walks and runs is your time divided by your distance.
Distance uses km or miles to match your weight unit. Forma does not estimate calories, heart rate or intensity, and days without an entry are unknown.
Workout calendar
A month view of the days with finished workouts.
The small number on a day is how many workouts you recorded that day. Pick a day to see its workouts.
An empty day only means nothing was recorded; it does not prove you did not train.
Your last 7 days
A summary of what you logged in the last 7 days: workouts, cardio time, food and weight.

Workouts are completed sessions next to the weekly plan you set. Calories are averaged over days that have a food entry. Weight change compares your earliest and latest weigh-ins within 30 days. A new best is a working set heavier than any before it, logged this week.
Days with no entry are unknown and are not counted as zero. These numbers describe your log; they are not advice to change what you eat or how you train.
Body measurements
Your weight and optional body measurements for the selected date.
Enter at least one value. Saving replaces that date\'s record, including any field left blank.
There is one record per date. Values show in the weight unit you chose in settings.
Recorded body weight
The weights you logged, over the last 90 days.
Each point is one recorded weight. Dates without a weight are not filled in; the line only joins real records.
The chart describes your records. It does not explain why your weight changed.
12-week training grid
Each square is one day of the last 12 weeks. Filled squares had a finished workout.
A stronger colour means two or more workouts that day. Today has an outline.
Empty squares are days without a record, not proof of rest.
Personal records
Your heaviest working set for each exercise, with an estimated one-rep max.
The best set is the highest load, then the most reps at that load. Sets without added load are not ranked.
Warm-ups are excluded. Records reflect what you logged.
Muscle map
A body diagram coloured by the working sets that involved each muscle in the last 7 days.
Counts come from finished workouts and the exercise catalog, with primary and supporting muscles kept separate.
Colours are not recovery or measured muscle activation.
Weekly review
A summary of the last 7 days: finished workouts, days with food entries, average logged calories and recorded weight.
Built from your records with fixed rules, offline. A weight comparison with the week before appears only when both weeks have at least 3 weights.
It never changes your targets or plan and does not explain the cause of weight changes.
Nutrition trends
Logged calories per day over the range you choose.
Days without entries are drawn as dashed outlines and left out of averages: they are unknown, not zero.
Comparisons use only targets you entered. Forma does not set or change them.
Training trends
Workouts, working sets and volume in rolling 7-day weeks.
Each bar is the 7 days ending on the date shown, counting finished workouts only. Volume is reps × added load, so bodyweight sets add sets but no volume.
This describes your log. It is not a training recommendation.
BMI
Body mass index from the height you entered and your latest logged weight.
Weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared.
BMI is a population screening number. It does not account for muscle, frame or age, and it is not a diagnosis.
Sleep
Nightly sleep duration and stages copied from your phone\'s health app (Health Connect or Apple Health).
Read-only, after you give permission. One source is used per night, and the copies stay separate from your Forma logs.
Missing nights are unknown. Forma does not score or assess sleep.
Records behind this review
The exact records the review used: workouts, meals and measurements with their dates.
Every number in the review is computed from these records, so you can check where it came from.
If something looks wrong, correct the record itself; the review updates.
Weekly check-in
A short weekly note: how many sessions you can fit next week and whether your food log feels complete.
If your number differs from your plan, Forma creates a proposal that you can confirm or cancel.
Nothing changes until you confirm.
Proposed schedule change
A change to your weekly session number that comes from your own check-in answer.
Confirm to apply it or cancel to keep your current number. Only the weekly number changes.
Exercises, loads and nutrition targets stay as recorded. This reflects your availability, not a prescribed program.
Optional local AI
On supported devices, on-device Gemini Nano can choose which already-computed facts to highlight.
It sees weekly statistics only, without your name, notes or meal descriptions. It runs on the device while the app is open, and nothing is sent online.
It cannot add claims or advice or change records. Everything else works without it.
This chart
Your recorded values over time.
Each point is an actual record. Missing dates are not filled in; lines only connect observations.
With a single record, the value is shown as text instead of a line.
